Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Group third quarter 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, the Q&A session will follow the standard format with one question and one follow-up per caller. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mark Gonzalez, Chief Risk Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Credit Officer; and Emily Santos, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Group delivered excellent results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on expanding our market share, improving our efficiency ratio, strengthening our balance sheet, investing in our people, driving innovation, and meeting our ESG goals.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our progress. First, our revenue diversification initiatives have significantly reduced reliance on net interest income, with non-interest revenues now comprising nearly half of total revenue, driven by robust growth in wealth management, payments, and capital markets fees across regions. Second, we've maintained a prudent asset sensitivity profile, remaining modestly asset-sensitive while deploying sophisticated hedges to manage interest rate risks effectively. Third, our net interest margin expanded to 3.45%, benefiting from loan repricing and securities optimization amid higher rates. Fourth, credit reserves saw a meaningful release, reflecting strong portfolio performance and forward-looking CECL modeling, with coverage ratios well above peers. Fifth, our capital position is rock-solid, with CET1 at 13.2% exceeding regulatory requirements across jurisdictions. And sixth, deposits grew steadily with a favorable mix shift toward savings products, supported by digital strategies and relationship banking.

These achievements position us exceptionally well for sustained growth. I will now turn the call over to Jennifer Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. UniBank Group reported net income of $1.8 billion for the third quarter, or $3.75 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 15% due to higher loan yields and controlled deposit costs. Non-interest income was up 28% year-over-year to $6.8 billion driven by growth in wealth management, payments, and corporate investment banking fees. Our efficiency ratio improved to 54%. We are on track to achieve our financial targets for the year.

Let me expand on these results and the key aspects Alex highlighted, starting with our revenue diversification initiatives and their impact. In this era of volatile interest rates, geopolitical tensions, and digital disruption, we've prioritized reducing our historical dependence on net interest income while scaling high-margin, recurring fee-based revenues. This strategy is delivering double-digit growth and bolstering our resilience. Total revenue for the year to date reached levels supporting full-year guidance of around $52 billion, up 8% year-over-year. Notably, net interest income now accounts for 52% of the mix, down from 68% three years ago, with non-interest income surging to 48%, a record. In Q3 alone, non-interest revenues hit $6.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year and representing 51% of quarterly total revenue. Our NIM held at 3.45%, aided by the Fed's higher-for-longer policy, but diversification has protected us from the 15-20 basis point compression peers like Wells Fargo and Bank of America have faced in deposit-heavy books.

Key drivers include our wealth management and asset management franchise, where we've expanded high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth offerings with a B2B2C approach similar to Goldman Sachs' Marcus but tailored uniquely. Assets under management grew 18% year-over-year to $1.2 trillion, with $45 billion in net new money. Fee income from advisory, custody, and alternatives like private credit and ESG funds rose 32% to $2.1 billion. Our UniWealth Prime app leverages AI-driven robo-advisory, akin to BlackRock's Aladdin, for personalized portfolios. Cross-sell to our 25 million retail customers hit 24%, up from 18%, adding $450 million in fees.

Payments and transaction services grew even faster at 35% year-over-year to $3.2 billion, surpassing Visa and Mastercard amid embedded finance trends. We've integrated APIs into platforms like Shopify and Salesforce, processing 2.5 billion transactions quarterly via real-time cross-border remittances on a blockchain ledger inspired by RippleNet, slashing settlement from T+2 to seconds and lifting take rates to 1.85%. In the U.S., UniPay digital wallet grabbed 12% P2P market share, competing with Venmo, while Stripe partnerships added $800 million in merchant acquiring. Margins here are 65%, far above traditional lending's 45%.

In corporate and investment banking, we've shifted to capital markets and advisory amid M&A slowdowns. ECM and DCM fees increased 22% to $1.1 billion, with our sustainable finance desk underwriting $15 billion in green bonds, tapping EU Taxonomy and the $1 trillion transition finance market. Structured products linked to volatility indices hedge VIX spikes post-Ukraine.

Regionally, North America, 55% of non-interest revenue, grew 25% on payments and wealth management amid strong consumer spending—UniCard charge volume up 20% despite Fed pauses. Europe grew 15% to $1.4 billion, offset by ESG advisory in our Dublin hub despite Basel IV and deposit shifts, with AUM up 12%. Asia-Pacific surged 45% to $1.2 billion, driven by $20 billion wealth inflows in Singapore and Hong Kong from China's HNWI migration and WeChat Pay integration, plus UPI in India adding 10 million digital accounts.

These align with digital acceleration—$1.2 billion invested in cloud-native platforms on AWS and Google Cloud for 99.99% uptime; ecosystem partnerships with 50+ fintech JVs; and risk-adjusted growth targeting 15-18% ROE at 12.5% CET1. Our three-year non-interest CAGR of 22% tops JPMorgan's 18% and Citigroup's 14%, per stress tests for 100bps rate drops by 2025. We see non-interest exceeding 55% of revenue by 2026, payments to $5 billion annually, adding $1.20 EPS this year.

Next, on asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management—a cornerstone of our balance sheet strength amid seven Fed hikes since 2022, with funds at 5.33% and an inverted SOFR curve. We've delivered $2.4 billion NII this quarter, up 18% year-over-year, at 11.8% CET1. We're modestly asset-sensitive, with +$185 million NII for +100bps shock over 12 months, net of hedges—a positive 8% repricing gap from our $450 billion commercial loans, 62% floating to SOFR. Deposits are 42% non-interest-bearing, beta at 35%.

In CCAR-like shocks, +200bps adds +$420 million or +12% NII; -100bps subtracts -$140 million or -4%, within 8% EAR tolerance. EVE sensitivity is +$2.1 billion for +100bps, duration gap +0.45 years (assets 3.2 vs. liabilities 2.75), overweight agency MBS at 4.8% yield.

Loan repricing hit 75% of C&I in six months at SOFR +225bps, up from +180bps, expanding NIM 25bps. Deposit beta at 38% in non-core prompted 4.75% CDs, average cost 1.9%. U.S. Midwest NII beta +15% on sticky deposits; Europe liability-sensitive via Frankfurt fixed mortgages but stable at ECB 4%; Asia neutral with swaps.

Our ALM Committee uses Quantum ALM platform with ML for convexity. Hedges: $15 billion including $8 billion receive-fixed swaps, $4 billion SOFR futures, $3 billion payer swaptions at 4.25%. EVaR under $1.8 billion at 99%, within limits. Aladdin overlays factor geopolitics.

Pivoting to growth-with-protection: SOFR-linked FlexRate Accounts for $50 billion inflows; adjustable CRE loans to 40%; $200 million AI prepayment analytics for $180 billion mortgages.

With steepening curve, 2024 NII tailwind $300-400 million even with cuts, asset-sensitive at +$160 million per 100bps.

Turning to NIM analysis, our 3.45% NIM rose 25bps quarter-over-quarter and 40bps year-over-year on ALM discipline despite deposit competition and inversion. On $285 billion earning assets up 8%, NII hit $2.48 billion, up 12% QoQ, from 42bps asset yield gain offset by 17bps cost rise.

Asset yields to 5.82%: 65% C&I at SOFR +250-300bps, SOFR up 35bps to 5.35%; $65 billion securities redeployed from 2.5% legacy to 5.1% agency MBS/FRNs, +15bps; loan mix to 55% C&I/CRE at 6.8% vs. 4.2% mortgages. U.S. Northeast +50bps; Europe 4.9%; Asia 3.2%.

Funding costs to 2.37%, beta 45% < peers. DDA 28%; CDs 65% beta at 4.8%; wholesale down to 5.1%. U.S. digital compression; Europe SONIA swaps.

Initiatives: AI dynamic pricing for 10% MMDA growth; $15 billion swaps for 3.30% floor; CRE de-risk to <5% office; treasury fees offset via UniCash.

Q4 guide 3.40-3.55%, +10bps if hikes, 3.20% if cuts, with 11.2% CET1 for buybacks.

On reserves and coverage: Q3 net PCL release $285 million, YTD $520 million vs. prior build. ACL $9.8 billion or 1.95% loans (up 5bps QoQ, 25bps YoY), >1.75-1.90% target, ahead of JPM/BofA.

Consumer (45% loans): $180 million release; cards delinq 2.1%, CO 3.8%; auto subprime down; PD -15-20bps on 4.2% unemployment, 3.5% savings.

CRE (22%): $50 million build; office $18 billion at 1.2x LTV, criticized 4.5%; multifamily offset; sold $2.5 billion, conc. 3.6%.

C&I (28%): $95 million release; NCO down 30%; energy/tech PD -10bps.

Regions: U.S. 2.05% coverage; Europe $20 million build LGD 35%; Asia $40 million release.

Ratios: NPL 0.85% (down 40bps YoY), ACL/NPL 229%; criticized 62%. CCAR pass 11.8%.

GenAI CECL with 50+ macros, NY Fed nowcast 12%; blockchain trade finance.

Release aids 12-14% ROE, $1.5 billion buybacks. H2 flat builds, CRE cap 5%.

Capital ratios: CET1 13.2% fully loaded (up 40bps QoQ, 110bps YoY), Tier 1 15.1%, total 18.5% on $452 billion RWAs (down 2%). > JPM/HSBC.

Reqs: Pillar 1 7.75% +2.0% G-SIB +1.25% ECB/Fed P2G =11.75%; +147bps, 200bps buffer.

U.S. 14.5% > Endgame; Europe 12.4% post €1.5B AT1; Asia 13.8%.

Drivers: $2.8B income +70bps; RWA efficiency $8B delever; pension 20bps.

Q4 13.4-13.6%; offset Basel IV 70% via optimization, M&A dry powder $10B. Targets 12-14% ROTE.

Finally, deposits: $285 billion, +4.2% QoQ, 7.8% YoY; core +6.1%. L/D 82%, NIM 3.65%.

Mix: Transactional 38% ($108B, -200bps); flat YoY commercial, Sunbelt +3%.

Savings 42% ($120B, +12% YoY, 4.75% APY > Ally/Marcus); Midwest 15%, PNW 10%.

Time 20% ($57B, +25% YoY, 5.10% CDs $4.2B); brokered <5%, beta 65%.

Beta 45%, top 20 8%. Strategies: AI Horizon Analytics + Plaid; 1.35x cross-sell; Sunbelt branches; vs. fintechs with AA- perks. H2 core +8-10%.

These elements drive our outperformance.

Mark Gonzalez:
Thank you, Jennifer. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility and commercial real estate exposures. We are taking proactive steps through enhanced stress testing, AI early warnings, and portfolio de-risking to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, including EVaR limits and macro overlays.

Robert Hayes:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 0.85% and criticized loans coverage at 62%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio across consumer, CRE, and C&I segments and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment, supported by robust ACL ratios and vintage performance.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. Our first question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the revenue diversification initiatives, particularly the regional differences and forward outlook?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, David. As Jennifer detailed, our shift has non-interest at 51% this quarter, with standout growth in payments and wealth management. North America led at 25%, Europe 15% despite Basel pressures via ESG, and Asia 45% on HNWI flows. Looking ahead, payments to $5 billion annually, non-interest over 55% by 2026, adding meaningful EPS while fortifying against rate drops.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for deposit growth and mix amid potential rate cuts?

Jennifer Lee:
Great question, Lisa. We've grown deposits 7.8% YoY to $285 billion, with savings up 12% on competitive 4.75% APYs and digital tools like auto-sweeps boosting acquisition 35%. Strategies include AI forecasting to cut churn, cross-sell for stickiness, Sunbelt expansion, and perks versus fintechs. Post-cuts, expect 8-10% core growth, funding 95% organically at low costs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
How are you addressing interest rate risk given the inverted curve?

Mark Gonzalez:
Thanks, Mike. Our asset-sensitive stance with hedges like $15 billion swaps and swaptions protects NII—+$185 million per 100bps up, -$140 million down within tolerances. Weekly ALM with Quantum platform and Aladdin scenarios covers non-parallel shifts and geopolitics, balancing 7-9% loan growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Wong:
Can you update us on reserve rationale, especially CRE?

Robert Hayes:
Absolutely, Sarah. The $285 million Q3 release reflects strong metrics—NPLs 0.85%, ACL 1.95% or 229% of NPLs. CRE build $50 million on office criticized up to 4.5%, but de-risked via $2.5 billion sales; multifamily offsets. CECL GenAI with Fed nowcasts ensures conservatism, passing CCAR at 11.8%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
